title: console-tooling-standup-2026-05-05
body:
Attendees: Maya (PM), Ravi (FE), Lina (BE), Owen (SRE), Jonah (Analytics)

Agenda:
- Quick sync on UI rollout work and canary strategy
- Analytics instrumentation progress and gap list
- Blockers for release and next steps

Notes:
- Ravi: UI feature flag scaffolding merged to feature/rollouts-v2; PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1892. Still need final e2e tests for auth flows (flaky). Local repro steps added to PR comments. Plan: fix flaky login in ticket PROD-427, aiming for Monday patch.

- Lina: Backend rollout API is stable on staging. Implemented batch rollout API endpoint and rate limiting per-tenant. Observed occasional 504s when attempting 5000 concurrent ops — Owen to investigate infra throttling. Deployed schema migration for rollout_jobs table, ran on staging, no regressions.

- Owen: SRE saw a spike in CPU on staging rollout controllers tied to big rollout jobs; increased horizontal autoscaling threshold for now. Will add autoscaling policy to terraform module (TF-592) and open a follow-up to tune metrics. Also confirmed KV cache eviction caused slowdowns for UI load tests; investigating possible cache pinning for rollout metadata.

- Jonah: Analytics instrumentation for route-level latency and token-level cost landed on backend (see PROD-412). Frontend is sending telemetry, but there's a mapping mismatch for the new route names (rollouts_v2 -> rollouts). Need a small transform in the pipeline (ETL job) to avoid gaps in dashboards. ETA: Jonah will patch ETL mapping by Friday.

Risks / Blockers:
- Auth e2e flakiness (PROD-427) blocks merging feature-flag gated UI rollout to prod. Developer note: add deterministic user fixture and avoid parallel session teardown in tests.
- 504s during large concurrent rollout ops — potential infra throttle; if not addressed could delay Dedicated customers using mass rollouts.
- Analytics mapping mismatch will affect last 24h of dashboards if not patched before next deploy.

Action Items / Owners:
- Ravi: stabilize e2e auth tests, add deterministic fixture, link to PR (due 2026-05-08).
- Lina: if Owen confirms throttle, add retry/backoff to rollout worker (due 2026-05-10).
- Owen: add autoscaling policy to terraform module and investigate KV pinning for rollout metadata (TF-592) (due 2026-05-07).
- Jonah: patch ETL mapping for route names and validate dashboards (due 2026-05-08).
- Maya: prepare canary rollout plan doc for exec review, include rollback thresholds and SLO targets (confluence draft link included in linked_artifacts).

Decisions Made:
- Canary will start at 1% traffic on Tuesday after auth tests pass, increase to 10% after 24h with no errors >5% and latency within SLO. Rollback policy: immediate rollback on errors>5% or token-cost delta >20% vs baseline.

Open Questions:
- Do we need per-tenant KV pinning or will aggressive cache warming suffice for now? (Action: Owen to propose design)
- Should analytics mapping transformation be deployed as a hotfix or bundled with the next release? Jonah prefers hotfix to avoid dashboard blindspots.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add a short checklist for on-call runbook when canary triggers rollback (Maya).
- Follow up with Customer Success about Dedicated customers expecting mass rollout behavior next week — Lina to sync.
- Link relevant Jira tickets in PR descriptions and Confluence playbook.

Meeting adjourned: 2026-05-05 10:25 PT

Informal / quick thoughts (brainstorm fragments):
- Consider a lightweight rollout simulator that can run locally against a staging cluster to simulate 1k+ rollouts without hitting prod infra — might help debug autoscaling.
- Could add a small telemetry field at rollout request level to tag expensive rollouts for post-mortem analysis.
- Need to document known flaky e2e tests in QA board so that release blocking checks can be traced.

Links / refs: see linked_artifacts for Confluence / Jira / PRs.

End of notes.
